heuristics.note: Code computes every answer: from a recipe, from the AI's spec (linear_equation, expand, signed_arithmetic, numeric_step) or from the slipped check problem for a retry. A proposal whose stated answer differs from code's, that has no unique solution, or whose numbers are out of range (|n| ≤ spec_number_limit, answers ≤ spec_answer_limit, denominators ≤ spec_denominator_limit) is rejected; a check problem whose single-number answer, or its opposite, is a number in it is rejected too (round 8 §3.6: practice problems may use any numbers). The AI never states a verdict; text that contradicts code's verdict is logged (round 7 §4), never changes the verdict, and is shown unchanged after code's own result line.

A check problem must match a recipe of its skill (the recipes used in reverse: exact structure, then the recipe's own validate()), use a number set not used in this session, not contain its own single-number answer or its opposite, and is worded by code. One that still contains its answer after one repair is replaced by a prepared check problem for the same skill, and the substitution is logged; every prepared problem satisfies the rule. Choice check problems come only from the contrast recipes. The card reads "Check question: on your own". HEURISTIC phrase audit before the card: a hint, method, strategy or reminder phrase (remember, make sure, don't forget, when you, hint, tip, careful, watch out, start by, same steps, like before, apply and similar) holds the attempt: it keeps its verdict and counts neither for nor against the goal; so does the check's answer when it comes from neither the previous problem (its numbers and answer) nor the student's entry. Neutral invitations (next, try, one more, another one, your turn, have a go), numbers the text shares with the check, and an answer that comes from earlier work are logged as signals only. Help during an open check (round 8 §3.1–§3.2): a reply whose move is HELP, HINT, EXPLAIN or ANSWER_QUESTION records help before it is shown, and the check becomes practice (an answer to it does not count and the run starts again); a reply with no help move whose text contains the check's expression, a number from it or its answer holds the check (HEURISTIC backstop: digits and number words); text with none of these records nothing.

HEURISTIC. Code reads standard notation itself, a number written in words (up to 999), and "3 = x" as x = 3. Every other entry (words, "×", "times", a letter standing alone between spaces, or anything code cannot read) is read by the AI. Code checks the reading: only numbers the student wrote (digits or number words), only the problem's variables the student wrote, at most 80 characters, and the drop check: the reading must re-express one stretch of the entry token for token, and nothing joined to it by an operation sign or word (plus, minus, times, divided by, over, negative), implicit multiplication or grouping may be left out; a change of grouping or operand order is rejected. Content joined only by "=" or a relation word may be left out (declared scope). When the reading fails, or plausible readings would be scored differently, nothing is graded and the student sees the AI's clarifying question. The shown result says "Read as …".

A slip is confirmed only when a recipe's slip signature matches: the structure is right and one lower-level calculation went wrong (7x + 25 for 7(x + 5)). The tutor may then ask one micro-question (code checks it) and offer a retry; the first slip in a run pauses the count, a second resets it; the slipped answer and the retry never count. A slip the structure contradicts (9x + 8 for 9(x + 8)) is never confirmed.

HEURISTIC DETECTORS; they log and do not block. Every learner-visible AI text is checked for the answer to an open or newly posed problem (as a number, number word, equivalent polynomial span or the key option's text; "one" as a determiner is not read as 1), internal vocabulary (expected answer, answer key, host, verdict, criterion and the like), a mastery or goal claim, a claim that work was done with or without help (not flagged in the last sentence before a check card, round 8 §3.4), and a contradiction of code's verdict. Two counters log only (round 8 §3.7): RESOLVE_AFTER_CORRECT (correct-answer feedback with an equation in the text on the way from the problem to its answer, or for linear equations a digit value of one of its sub-expressions at the solution, other than the problem, the student's answer and the student's numbers) and VALUE_QUESTION_IN_TEXT (a question sentence with a value cue and some mathematics while no problem is posed). Each finding is recorded with the exact text, the guard and the problem and response it relates to; the student sees the text unchanged. Paraphrased answers are not detected. Only envelope and problem-acceptance failures are repaired (once); if the repair fails too, the turn is held with a retry.

Two choices: a hint, or "I haven't learned this yet" (round 7 §6.4). Help is recorded before any AI call, and an answer after it resets the run. Typed text is never classified as stuck: "idk" or "???" is a message to the tutor (round 7 §6.3); help is then recorded only if the tutor's reply carries a help move (round 8 §3.1).

Deterministic matching of each recipe's known error patterns (e.g. the factor multiplied only the x). A match is recorded as an observation, never a confirmed cause; the AI sees it and chooses what to do.

One AI call per turn with the full context, built anew; two when an entry must be read first; one repair at most. The first turn of a session also makes the architecture-binding call. Reasoning per call (per_call): enabled at low effort for a reading, a wrong answer with no signature, or a free-text message about maths; disabled otherwise. Each call is logged with its purpose and reasoning setting.

A code is created with the first recorded answer of a session and its record is updated in the same database transaction as every later commit. The record holds, per skill, a status (goal met, needed help, unresolved, not in the beta), a date and observed mistake-pattern codes, plus the route target, the tutor's stated next focus and the next skill; no answers, names or addresses. The server stores only the sha256 of a code. 12 characters from 31 symbols give about 59.4 bits. One live session per code; entering it on another device takes the session over. Lookups: one generic message, at most 10 failures per hour per browser session. Records are deleted progress_retention_days (default 90) after their last use. Results from earlier sessions never count toward this session's goals. Codes do not carry between the beta and this install (separate databases).

One HTML file (algebra-report-YYYY-MM-DD.html) with inline CSS, no scripts and no external requests; the four learner headings, the teacher details expanded, the audit list, the date and the progress code. Every sentence is written by code from the gradebook.

owner_rule_overrides.note: A check answer given after "I'm stuck" (a hint), or after a tutor reply with a help move during the check, resets the count of correct answers in a row to 0, exactly as a wrong answer does. Round 6 records of an explanation or a typed stuck phrase count the same way.
